key_insight: QuFrame is a quantum-control microarchitecture designed to track Pauli frames in real time and close the quantum error-correction loop within 1 μs.
engineering_relevance: It addresses time-critical control dependencies introduced by non-Clifford magic-state gadgets while sustaining QPU-rate throughput.
method: QuFrameISA separates instruction execution from continuous Pauli frame management.
Per-qubit Instruction Resolution Engines use a single table lookup, while a Pauli Frame Management Unit supports independent, lock-free concurrent commits.
An asynchronous primary decoder is paired with an on-chip fallback decoder and hardware reconciliation of divergent updates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 144 ns fallback decoding and a 1 μs QEC-loop deadline without degraded logical error rates, but provides no benchmark or implementation details.
watch_item: Scalability and timing guarantees need validation under realistic decoder workloads and distributed-control communication delays.
paper_title: QuFrame: Pauli Frame Tracking for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Control
